detail.critique: The claim that Microsoft acquired Builder.ai in 2025 is contradicted by multiple independent sources, including the New York Times, which describe only a partnership; bankruptcy filings in May‑June 2025 show the company was insolvent and not acquired; no Microsoft press release or SEC filing evidences an acquisition; thus the claim is false.

detail.runner_up_case: The strongest honest case for TRUE rests on Microsoft's uniquely deep entanglement with Builder.ai: Microsoft led its Series D, served as its strategic cloud partner, and every collapse narrative describes the company as 'Microsoft-backed' — exactly the kind of relationship that gets misreported as ownership. If 'acquired' captured a real 2025 transfer — an acqui-hire of the engineering team, or a court-approved sale of Engineer.ai's assets out of the 2 June 2025 Delaware Chapter 7 estate to Microsoft — the claim would be TRUE as stated, and nothing in the gathered record affirmatively excludes an asset-side deal, because no one has checked Microsoft's own SEC filings or the bankruptcy sale docket for a purchaser. That said, this is a possibility argument, not affirmative evidence: every dated, high-weight source (NYT 2025-08-31; Bloomberg 2025-06-05) describes a partnership plus a liquidation with creditors seizing accounts, and the company's own insolvency announcement of 20 May 2025 is inconsistent with a completed acquisition. TRUE is therefore a long shot, but it is not logically excluded by the record as assembled.
would_flip_it: An official Microsoft press release, blog post, or 8-K/10-K business-combinations note (FY2025) naming Builder.ai or Engineer.ai as an entity or asset acquisition completed in 2025.

A Delaware bankruptcy court order in the Engineer.ai Corp. Chapter 7 case (filed 2025-06-02) approving a sale of Builder.ai's assets, business, or team to Microsoft, or credible reporting of such a sale to Microsoft as purchaser.

Post-August-2025 reporting from a tier-one outlet (Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ, NYT) stating that Microsoft completed an acquisition of Builder.ai or its core assets in 2025, superseding the partnership-and-liquidation narrative.
A Microsoft SEC filing or executive statement disclosing that the May 2023 'partnership/lead investment' was restructured into full ownership during 2025.
